title: CI regression watchdog: throughput (tokens/sec) + p95 latency guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: PRs that touch the serving runtime or kernel selection occasionally introduce regressions in serving throughput (tokens/sec) or 95th percentile latency. Existing CI runs smoke/throughput jobs but lack a robust, repeatable baseline + statistical gating strategy, leading to false positives from noise and missed slow degradations.

Goal: Ship a CI-level 'regression watchdog' job that automatically compares a PR's performance profile against a calibrated baseline and blocks merges when statistically significant regressions are detected (configurable SLOs and thresholds). The check must be low-friction for contributors and actionable for on-call.

Core acceptance criteria:
- CI job (GitHub Actions) named perf-watchdog runs on PRs touching runtime code paths and on scheduled weekly baseline jobs.
- Collects metrics: sustained tokens/sec (median & 10th percentile), p95 latency (ms), and error rate.
- Baseline generation: deterministic runner against last-green commit with 30 warmup runs, 100 steady-state samples (configurable), and automatic artifact upload to S3.
- Regression logic: fail PR when (a) tokens/sec drops by >= 6% with p < 0.01 (bootstrap CI) OR (b) p95 latency increases by >= 8% with p < 0.01. Thresholds adjustable via repo config.
- Noise mitigation: compare distributions (bootstrap), apply outlier trimming (median absolute deviation), and require reproducibility by re-running the PR job once before final block.
- Artifacts: perf artifacts (raw samples, summary CSVs, flamegraph link) uploaded and linked in PR check; Grafana perf-summary dashboard links included.
- Documentation: runbook and triage checklist added to Confluence; owners and on-call notified for gated failures.

Design decisions + trade-offs:
- Statistical test: we chose non-parametric bootstrap for distributions because runtime metrics are non-normal and sample sizes are modest. This costs compute time but reduces false signals compared to simple percent-delta checks.
- Sample size: 100 steady-state samples strikes a balance between CI runtime and statistical power. If a PR contains only small changes, contributors can opt into a 'fast' mode (30 samples) but this will only produce advisory warnings, not blocking failures.
- Warmup: kernels and caching behavior require explicit warmup. We run 30 warmup iterations to stabilize KV cache and JIT paths. This adds ~5 minutes but drastically reduces variance.
- Baseline drift: week-over-week model and infra changes cause baseline drift. We will maintain a moving baseline (weekly recalibration job) and store revision-tagged baselines to allow historical comparisons.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Create perf-checker GH Action that can run on PR or schedule. Uses the existing perf harness binary (perf-runner) with flags for warmup/samples and outputs ndjson of per-iteration metrics.
2) Runner uploads raw artifacts to s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/{repo}/{sha}/ and writes a summary JSON with median/tail stats.
3) Baseline job (scheduled, weekly) updates baseline pointer in S3 and writes metadata (commit, infra spec). Baseline recalibration reviewed by owners.
4) PR job fetches baseline, runs perf-runner, computes bootstrap confidence intervals for delta in tokens/sec and p95 latency (we'll reuse the perf-analysis lib). If regression meets gating criteria, the check initially marks 'action_required' and triggers an automatic one-retry run. If still failing, the check fails and posts summary + links to artifacts and the triage runbook.
5) Add Grafana panel that aggregates CI-run artifacts for morning health checks and a lightweight Canary alert that flags sustained drift across multiple PRs.

Operational concerns / open questions:
- CI runner variability: different GH runners (shared hosted) add noise. We'll pin perf jobs to a small fleet of dedicated self-hosted runners with fixed GPU/hardware profiles (dedicated-perf-1..3).
- Cost: steady-state sampling and dedicated runners increase CI cost. We'll monitor cost and may gate full blocking checks to PRs that touch critical paths only (files under /runtime /kernels /serve).
- Interactions with Dedicated customers or private deployments: ensure no customer data leaves artifacts and use sanitized input prompts.

Deliverables / docs to add:
- Confluence doc: "CI Perf Watchdog: design + thresholds" (link placeholder).
- Runbook: "triage-perf-watchdog" with checklist and owner rotation.
- GH Action and perf-analysis library code with unit tests and a small e2e in staging.

comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Initial spike completed. Confirmed bootstrap-based comparison reduces false-positive rate vs simple delta on our test harness (ran 1200 synthetic runs). Documents updated in Confluence draft.

2025-02-18 - Arjun Patel: Prototype GH Action written (perf-watchdog/action.yml). Uses self-hosted perf runners perf-host-1/2. Preliminary thresholds adjusted to 6%/8% after observing noise during kernel warmup windows.

2025-02-22 - Lena Gomez (QA): Observed sporadic p95 spikes correlated with autoscaler activity on shared infra. We are switching to pinned perf runners and adding environment tags to artifacts for easier filtering.
2025-02-26 - Arjun Patel: Implemented one-retry policy for PR failures. Added outlier trimming via 3*MAD before bootstrap. Running smoke across recent PRs to verify false-positive rate < 3%.
2025-03-01 - Maya Chen: Roadblocked by missing perf-analysis C lib for bootstrap; landed a minimal Python fallback until C library is ready. Next: add dashboard panels and update runbook.
